newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan insurance market up, but growth elusive.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan insurance market up, but growth elusive.

text.p: Morocco's insurance market saw growth of 8.75 percent in net premiums to 6.8 billion dirhams ($785 million) in 1995, an industry spokesman said on Tuesday.

"This result may appear encouraging after a year of heavy stagnation, but must however be viewed with caution because it was not a real relaunch of the insurance market," the Moroccan Federation of Insurance and Reinsurance Societies said.
Total premiums in 1994 were 6.284 billion dirhams.

In its report for the year, the federation said vehicle insurance premiums, which accounted for some 40 percent of total premium income, grew 17 percent over 1994, while the number of vehicles on the road rose by nine percent.
It attributed the rise in premium revenue largely to increased tariffs, introduced in September 1994 and again one year later.
Fire insurance, making up 5.6 percent of company business, recorded a negative growth of 0.47 percent, falling to 383.7 million dirhams against 385.6 in 1994.

Civil liability insurance premiums grew to 114.8 million dirhams in 1995 compared with 111.8 million the year before, but were "not enough to regain the level of 1993 of 130.4 million dirhams", the federation said.
For the second consecutive year, marine insurance fell, to 464.9 million dirhams against 466.4 million in 1994 and 472.7 million the year before.

"Besides the heavy fall in premiums attributable to companies put into liquidation, this situation results from the crisis which for several years has affected the activities of the fishing industry and cautious attitude of insurance companies towards this form of cover," the report added.
